subject: general
question: The Hindu temples 'Hinglaj Mata' and 'Katasraj' are located in which neighbouring country of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu temple **Hinglaj Mata** is located in the Hingol National Park in Balochistan, Pakistan, and is an important pilgrimage site for Hindus.
 
• The **Katasraj Temples**, also known as the Katas Raj Temples, are a complex of ancient Hindu temples located near Chakwal in Punjab, Pakistan.
 
• The Katasraj Temples are associated with Hindu mythology, believed to have been built around a sacred pond that was formed from the tears of Lord Shiva after the death of his wife, Sati.
 
• Hinglaj Mata is one of the **Shakti Peethas**, revered as holy sites where parts of Goddess Sati's body are believed to have fallen, as per Hindu mythology.
 
• Both Hinglaj Mata and Katasraj Temples are significant cultural and religious landmarks, attracting pilgrims from India and other countries despite political boundaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hinglaj Mata Shakti Peetha:**

 
 
• Hinglaj Mata is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, where it is believed the head of Goddess Sati fell during Lord Shiva's Tandava.
 
• The site is located in a desert region and is visited by thousands of Hindu pilgrims annually, including during the Hinglaj Yatra.
 
• It is unique in that it is housed in a natural cave rather than a man-made structure.
 
 
 
• **Katasraj Temples:**
 
 
• The Katasraj complex includes several temples, some dating back to the Mahabharata era.
 
• The sacred pond, called **Katas**, is believed to have healing properties and is a major feature of the site.
 
• It is mentioned in Hindu texts like the Puranas and is also linked to the Pandavas' exile in Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Religious Tolerance and Cultural Preservation in Pakistan:**
 
 
• Despite being a Muslim-majority country, Pakistan has preserved several Hindu and Sikh religious sites under its cultural heritage policies.
 
• Efforts are made to maintain these sites for religious pilgrims and as a part of the shared cultural history of the region.
 
 
 
• **Hindu Pilgrimage in Pakistan:**
 
 
• Hinglaj Mata and Katasraj Temples are among the key destinations for Hindu pilgrims traveling to Pakistan.
 
• Special arrangements are often made for pilgrims, including visas and security, under the bilateral agreements between India and Pakistan.
